_readme: Copy this file to clients/<name>.json (that folder is gitignored AND .vercelignore'd — it holds live credentials).
Fill in every value marked <...>, then run:  npm run go-live -- <name>
slug            → the Vercel project name and the client's URL label (lowercase, digits, hyphens).
vercel.token    → the client's Vercel account → Settings → Tokens → Create (any scope, no expiry).
vercel.project  → optional; a different Vercel project name than the slug.
subdomain       → the first part of the cafe's address: <subdomain>.<apex> (apex = clients/_platform.json). Add the DNS records the console shows after the first run.

cloudflare      → OPTIONAL (realtime nudges). Leave null and the cafe simply polls, exactly as it does today. token → the CLIENT'S OWN Cloudflare account → My Profile → API Tokens → Create. The FIRST deploy creates the Worker AND runs the Durable Object migration, so it needs a token that can CREATE Workers (Workers Scripts:Edit on an Admin-level token); later code-only updates fit a narrower one. Cloudflare's docs do NOT state which scope a DO migration needs — see DEPLOY.md for the measured answer. Like vercel.token and mongodbUri, this is the client's own account: they sign up, they own it, they can revoke the token at any time and everything else keeps running.
mongodbUri      → the client's Atlas M0 SRV string; MUST end with the database name (…mongodb.net/pos?…). Network Access: 0.0.0.0/0.
admin.password  → at least 8 chars with a digit and a special character. Hand it to the client, they change it on first login.
tables          → REQUIRED: a count (T-1..T-n) or a list of names — the floor plan is this cafe's own data. menu → optional starter menu; the client can import a CSV later.
image           → null (no product photos yet — everything else works) or an R2 / Cloudinary block, see DEPLOY.md.
generated       → written by the tool (secrets, project id, host). Leave it alone; deleting it would rotate secrets.

standbyHosts    → optional: the SAME cafe on other Vercel accounts (same database/images/logins, own *.vercel.app URL). [{ "label": "standby", "vercel": { "token": "<token from that account>", "project": null, "teamId": null } }] — run with --host standby.
